title: A clean Windows 11 host goes from no Python to a passing /kb-setup, on record
goal: kb/_self/reports/windows-fresh-host.md records one run on a temporary clean local account on the Windows 11 host (Git for Windows, no Python for that account): install-python.ps1's preflight and install output and every /kb-setup step that needs no Claude Code sign-in, run by its command as that account, with a final line result: pass; every failure found on the way is filed as a bug.

gates.question: Which clean Windows 11 host should the from-scratch /kb-setup run on?
options: Windows Sandbox on a Windows 11 Pro machine
gates.recommendation: Windows Sandbox on a Windows 11 Pro machine
gates.answer: Windows Sandbox on a Windows 11 Pro machine

gates.question: How far should the unattended clean-host run go, given Claude Code must be signed in as the new account for /kb-setup and credentials are never copied?
options: all but the sign-in, on a temporary local account
gates.recommendation: all but the sign-in, on a temporary local account
gates.answer: everything for environment setup, but not the Claude part; no manual action by the operator

notes: Windows Sandbox (the earlier gate answer) is off on this host and needs a reboot; a temporary local standard account is the clean profile an unattended session can make. The Claude Code sign-in, MCP registration and calls, and the query log question stay out of the run.
